procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - ADHD
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Routine stimulant check. Pharmacy switch in December went fine. No new symptoms. Headaches 1-3 a month. Says he has cut back drinking "a little" since the fall but describes the same weekend pattern. Smoking unchanged.
O: Vitals per flowsheet - normal BP and HR. Alert, pleasant. Heart RRR. Lungs clear.
A/P: ADHD - stable, continue methylphenidate ER 36 mg, PMP reviewed. Post-concussive sx - stable. Alcohol/tobacco - brief counseling again, he is precontemplative. RTC 3 mo.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Patient did not arrive for 3:00 follow-up. Called cell, left voicemail to reschedule. Next methylphenidate fill due ~4/20.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - ADHD follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Missed 4/10 - was called in for overtime on a job, forgot to cancel. Came in before work today.
No complaints. Med working, no cardiac sx. Mood fine. Headaches occasional.
Vitals reviewed, unremarkable. Exam: heart regular, lungs clear, neuro grossly normal.
Plan: continue methylphenidate ER 36 mg qAM and sertraline 50 mg. Still smoking a ppd, not ready to quit. Physical in the fall.

documents.title: Early refill request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Patient called asking for methylphenidate refill; last 30-day fill 7/26 per PMP. He says he wants it before a week-long job out of town. Reviewed agreement with him - fills no sooner than 2 days early. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: RE: Early refill request
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Not filling 2 weeks early. Will send on 8/23 as usual; pharmacy can hold it for pickup when he's back. RN to let him know.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
22M, yearly exam.

No interval illness. ADHD steady on methylphenidate ER 36. Sertraline 50, mood good. Post-concussive headaches roughly twice monthly, ibuprofen works. Wrist fine.
Tobacco 1 ppd, now about 3-4 years. Alcohol same binge pattern, 2-3 nights/wk, 5-6 drinks; no further legal trouble per pt.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Well-appearing. HEENT normal, TMs clear. Neck supple, no thyromegaly. Cardiac RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Abd soft, nontender, no hepatomegaly. Skin clear. Neuro: CN intact, strength 5/5, gait steady.
Screens: PHQ-9 3, GAD-7 1, AUDIT-C 8.

A/P:
1. Preventive - Tdap today (last 2013) and flu vaccine. CBC and CMP for liver numbers given the drinking.
2. Alcohol - binge pattern persists. Reviewed risk with stimulant and with driving. Offered referral; declines.
3. Tobacco - advised to quit, declines NRT.
4. ADHD and post-concussive syndrome - stable, no changes.
RTC 3-4 months for med check.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Josue - blood count and chemistry panel from Wednesday are normal, including the liver enzymes. Good news, but the drinking is still the thing I'd most like to help you with when you're ready.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Telehealth - medication check
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, pt at home, ID confirmed.
Methylphenidate ER 36 mg continues to work, no side effects. Sleep ok. Mood ok on sertraline. Headaches not more frequent. Smoking a pack daily; drinking unchanged by his account.
Assessment: ADHD stable. Post-concussive syndrome stable.
Plan: continue both meds, monthly stimulant scripts after PMP check. In-person visit in spring.

events.reason: Right hip pain after motor vehicle collision

conditions.label: Posterior dislocation of right hip, initial encounter

documents.title: Emergency Department Record (outside)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 04/06/2025. Received 04/30/2025 in response to records request.

CC: R hip pain after MVC.
HPI: 22 yo M arrived by EMS after a high-speed crash; he was the front passenger, no seatbelt. Per EMS the vehicle hit a guardrail and spun off the road into a ditch. Awake and talking on scene. Complains of severe right hip pain, could not stand. Denies striking his head, denies LOC, denies abdominal pain.
PMH ADHD, prior mild TBI at 19 with post-concussive syndrome. PSH L distal radius ORIF, T&A. Meds methylphenidate ER 36 qAM, sertraline 50 daily, ibuprofen 600 prn. NKDA. Smokes 1 ppd. Drinks heavily on weekends.

Exam: GCS 15. No scalp or facial injury. C-spine cleared clinically. Chest and abdomen atraumatic, nontender. Pelvis stable. R lower extremity shortened, hip held internally rotated; any passive movement painful. No thigh swelling, deformity, wound or bleeding. Sensation intact in sciatic, femoral and obturator distributions; DP/PT pulses 2+; foot dorsiflexion and plantarflexion intact.

Imaging: AP pelvis - right femoral head displaced posteriorly and superiorly out of the acetabulum, consistent with posterior hip dislocation. No fracture seen.
Orthopedics consulted from the ED.

Procedure: closed reduction of R hip under procedural sedation by ED with orthopedics at bedside, successful on first attempt. Tolerated well.
Post-reduction AP pelvis: concentric reduction. CT pelvis post-reduction: right hip concentrically reduced; no acetabular or femoral head fracture; no intra-articular fragment.
Post-reduction neurovascular exam unchanged, intact.

Disposition: discharged home 09:50 with crutches, WBAT, posterior hip precautions reviewed (no deep flexion, no crossing legs, no internal rotation). Continue home ibuprofen for pain. Orthopedics clinic in 1-2 weeks. Seatbelt counseling given.
Dx: posterior dislocation of right hip, reduced.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Patient call - ED visit over the weekend
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt calling. Was a passenger in a car crash early Sunday morning, his right hip "popped out" and they put it back in at the ED and sent him home. On crutches. Pain manageable with ibuprofen. No numbness in leg or foot, no head injury. Needs a note for work and wants to be seen. ED told him to see ortho, he has a number to call. Booked with PCP Wed 4/9. Advised ED for new numbness, worsening pain, or foot weakness.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - post-ED follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
22M seen after ED visit on 4/6. No ED records yet - history from patient.
He was the front passenger; not belted. Right hip dislocated, reduced in the ED under sedation, told no fracture on x-ray and CT. Sent home same morning on crutches.
Since then: hip sore but better each day, ibuprofen 600 two or three times a day helps. Using crutches, putting some weight on the leg. No numbness, tingling or foot drop. Didn't hit his head. No headache beyond his usual.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Uncomfortable getting on table. R hip - no bruising over the lateral thigh, ROM deferred. Sensation intact to light touch R foot and leg, ankle dorsiflexion and great toe extension 5/5, DP pulse 2+.

A/P: R posterior hip dislocation s/p closed reduction 4/6.
- Ortho follow-up - he has the clinic number, will call today. Reviewed hip precautions.
- Pain: ibuprofen 600 q6h prn with food, max 4/day; short course ok.
- Work note: off work through ortho visit.
- Requesting ED record.
- Seatbelt - every time. He agreed.
RTC after ortho, ~6-8 wk.

documents.title: Work note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: To whom it may concern: Josue Hernandez was seen in this office today for an injury. He is unable to work until cleared by orthopedics, expected within 2-3 weeks. Please contact the office with any questions about his return.

documents.title: Orthopedic Clinic Letter (outside)
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Outside orthopedics group. Visit 04/23/2025. Received 05/01/2025.

Re: Josue Hernandez, DOB 08/31/2002

Thank you for following this patient. He is a 22 year old seen 17 days after closed reduction of a right posterior hip dislocation from a car crash. He has been walking with crutches, partial weight, and the pain is steadily better.

Exam: walks with crutches, mild antalgic gait. R hip flexion to 90 with mild discomfort at end range, internal rotation not tested per precautions. No sciatic nerve deficit: EHL, tibialis anterior and gastrocnemius 5/5, sensation intact in the foot. Distal pulses palpable.
AP pelvis today: right hip concentrically reduced. No fracture.

Impression: right posterior hip dislocation, simple, status post closed reduction, recovering as expected.
Plan: wean off crutches over the next 1-2 weeks as comfort allows. Posterior precautions to 6 weeks from injury. Light duty may begin now (no ladders, no lifting over 20 lb); full duty from 05/19/2025. Return to this clinic as needed.
Meds: methylphenidate ER, sertraline, ibuprofen prn. Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: ED record received
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: ED record from 4/6 visit received by fax after second request. Filed under the ED encounter and routed to PCP.

documents.title: Outside ED record reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: ED record reviewed. Simple posterior R hip dislocation, closed reduction first pass, CT after reduction with no fracture or loose fragment. Matches what he told me. Ortho appt is 4/23.

documents.title: Work note for full duty
documents.author: patient
documents.body: My boss wants a note from you saying I can go back to full duty Monday. The bone doctor said the 19th. hip is pretty much fine now, off the crutches

documents.title: RE: Work note for full duty
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad to hear it. I have the orthopedic letter clearing you for full duty from 5/19 - a note saying so is attached under Letters. Still keep up the hip precautions until about 5/18.

documents.title: Return to work note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: To whom it may concern: Josue Hernandez is cleared by his orthopedic surgeon to return to full duty without restrictions as of 05/19/2025. Please call the office if you need anything further.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Interval: ortho saw him 4/23, letter reviewed - reduction holding, no nerve injury. Back to full duty since 5/19. No hip pain, walking and climbing ladders without trouble.
ADHD med check: methylphenidate ER 36 mg working. Mood fine on sertraline. Headaches as usual.
Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Normal gait, R hip full painless ROM, neurovascularly intact distally.
A/P: R hip dislocation - recovered. ADHD - continue current dose, PMP ok. Tobacco and alcohol - brief advice, declines. Physical in the fall.
